state.purpose: Advisory assessment of a Codex skill model refresh. These are supplied research facts and proposed choices, not measured task outcomes. Jev is not browsing, coding, authorizing actions, or certifying model quality.
user_priorities: Keep Astra as the sole controller for coordinated work.
Tiny deterministic work stays Direct with zero delegation.
Reduce maintenance and unnecessary approval pauses without weakening scope, ownership or real verification.
The user requested research on newly released GPT-6 Sol and Luna, followed by iteration of the skill.

current_candidate.controller: gpt-6-astra / high, independent controller is read-only
current_candidate.specialist: gpt-5.6-sol / high, difficult separable implementation or targeted review
current_candidate.regular: gpt-5.6-terra / high, routine implementation, testing and integration under settled requirements
current_candidate.efficient: gpt-5.6-luna / max, mechanical batches with objective verification
current_candidate.coordination: Choose only needed workers directly. No mandatory chain through every model. Workers are leaves. One active writer per scope. Missing evidence is usually FIX, not a fresh authorization request.
current_candidate.validation: Existing candidate is uninstalled and unpublished. Historical probes exist but there is no matched quality, latency or total-cost comparison using the new Sol and Luna.

official_evidence.fact: GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna were released on September 22, 2026.

GPT-6 Sol is positioned for complex coding and agentic workflows. Supports high reasoning effort and reasoning with tools through Responses. Standard short-context input/output prices are USD 2/10 per million tokens.

GPT-6 Luna is positioned for focused high-volume tasks. Supports max reasoning effort and reasoning with tools through Responses. Standard short-context input/output prices are USD 0.10/0.50 per million tokens.

At the same Standard short-context processing tier, old Sol input/output is USD 4/20, Terra 2/12 and old Luna 0.20/1.20 per million tokens. New Sol has equal input price and lower output price than Terra. These rates alone establish no task-quality, elapsed-time, token-volume or ChatGPT-credit result.
Migration guidance says to preserve current effective reasoning effort where supported and compare results on representative tasks when changing it.

options.staged_refresh: Upgrade specialist to GPT-6 Sol high and efficient to GPT-6 Luna max. Keep Astra and Terra and all role IDs/scopes. Validate real calls and current task boundaries. Evaluate merging the two execution tiers separately; do not claim new performance savings yet.
options.three_tier_now: Immediately make Astra controller, GPT-6 Sol the combined routine/difficult executor, and GPT-6 Luna the efficient executor. Retain Terra only as an explicitly selected compatibility option. Fewer default routing distinctions, but routine replacement lacks matched task evidence.
options.effort_reduction_now: Upgrade Sol and Luna and lower Luna's default effort from max to medium immediately to target latency. Current workflow has no comparison showing acceptable quality at the lower effort.
options.wait_for_full_benchmark: Do not change active source defaults until a broad cross-project benchmark is complete. Minimizes default changes but delays narrow, testable adoption.

representative_cases: A one-line button label change: deterministic, no delegation value.
Mechanical JSON cleanup across many files: remove one exact top-level key while preserving nested content and unrelated fields.
Routine pagination feature with established interfaces and boundary tests.
Difficult installer recovery review: a rollback move can fail after a transaction partially changes files; original recoverable copies must survive.
Two agents request overlapping writes: only one active writer, independent readers may proceed.
Worker declares PASS but required verification is absent: obtain the missing check within existing authority.

first_iteration.instructions: Which proposed option in `options` is the most defensible next source iteration given `user_priorities`, `current_candidate` and `official_evidence`? Evaluate adoption speed, scope preservation and current evidence together, not just token rates.
